haiku-low.q1: captured_amount_cents minus the sum of amount_cents for pending and succeeded refunds. The page shows this only as a guide; step 3 does the real check.
haiku-low.q2: Retry with the same Idempotency-Key up to 3 times (4 attempts total), with about 1s, 2s and 4s backoff plus jitter. If all fail, submit_state becomes unconfirmed and status stays pending.
haiku-low.q3: It stops immediately with no retry. submit_state becomes rejected, the provider message is stored, and the refund transitions to failed, releasing the amount.
haiku-low.q4: A transition to succeeded, from a webhook (step 8) or the reconciler (step 9), creates an email_outbox row. The unique refund_id ensures the email is queued only once.
haiku-low.q5: It is computed on every read: succeeded refunds total versus captured amount. Partially refunded when 0 < total < captured, Refunded when equal. It changes only when a refund succeeds.
haiku-low.q6: A SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the payment row so transactions run one at a time. Under the lock, pending and succeeded refunds are summed and checked against the remaining amount.
haiku-low.q7: The key is refunds.id, a UUID generated when the row is inserted in step 3. It is stored on the row and reused for every retry and resend.
haiku-low.q8: webhook_events is unique on provider_event_id, so duplicates are stored once. Status updates are guarded by status = pending, so repeats change nothing; contradictions are marked conflict. email_outbox is unique on refund_id.
haiku-low.q9: It stays pending, because a timed-out or 5xx provider call may have created the refund. The amount stays reserved, and the reconciler later resolves it.
haiku-low.q10: A reconciler job runs every 15 minutes on pending refunds with next_check_at due. Succeeded or failed transitions the refund; still pending is logged and rechecked later, growing from 1h to 6h.
haiku-low.q11: The page shows Pending, sending to provider, and polls GET /admin/refunds/:id every few seconds. Later it shows accepted-by-provider pending status, or failed with the provider's message.

sonnet.q1: captured_amount_cents minus the sum of amount_cents of that payment's refunds with status pending or succeeded (failed ones don't count). Page value is only a guide; step 3 does the real check.
sonnet.q2: The worker retries with the same Idempotency-Key, up to 3 retries (4 attempts total), backoff about 1s, 2s, 4s plus jitter, 10s timeout per attempt. The same key makes a retry return the original refund rather than a second one. If all fail, the refund becomes submit_state unconfirmed, status stays pending.
sonnet.q3: No retry. Go to 5b: submit_state = rejected, provider_message set to the provider's error text, transition to failed (actor system:worker) with audit refund.failed. The amount is released since failed refunds don't count. Admin sees Failed with the provider's message verbatim.
sonnet.q4: A transition of the refund to succeeded (via webhook in step 8 or reconciler in step 9) inserts an email_outbox row (queued) in the same transaction; an email worker then sends the email. Only once because refund_id is unique in email_outbox.
sonnet.q5: succeeded_total = sum of amount_cents of the payment's refunds with status succeeded. 0 means no label; 0 < total < captured_amount_cents means Partially refunded; total = captured_amount_cents means Refunded. Pending and failed refunds don't change it. It is computed on every read of the order, nothing stored, so it changes when a refund becomes succeeded.
sonnet.q6: In the step 3 transaction, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the payment row so concurrent admins are handled one after the other. With the lock held it computes the sum of pending and succeeded refunds (READ COMMITTED sees refunds committed while waiting), checks amount <= captured minus sum, then inserts the pending refund row. The second admin gets 409 if the amount exceeds what remains.
sonnet.q7: The key is refunds.id (a UUID) of our refund row, created in step 3 before the provider is called. It is sent as the Idempotency-Key header on each attempt, including retries, worker resends after lease expiry, and reconciler resends (safe within 24 hours of first_submitted_at, reconciler uses about 22 hours).
sonnet.q8: Webhook_events.provider_event_id is unique: a duplicate delivery returns 200 and stops. Status changes go through transition(), whose UPDATE has AND status = 'pending', so a terminal state can't be overwritten: same-status repeat changes 0 rows and the event is marked processed; a contradicting event is marked conflict, audited as refund.webhook_conflict and support is alerted. The email is only once because the outbox row is created only on transition to succeeded and refund_id is unique there. (Email service could still send twice if the worker crashes between sending and marking sent, unless it accepts refund_id as idempotency key.)
sonnet.q9: submit_state = unconfirmed with status kept pending, because we don't know whether the provider created the refund; keeping pending keeps the amount reserved. next_check_at = now + 15 min, audit refund.submit_unconfirmed; the reconciler (step 9) resolves it.
sonnet.q10: The reconciler, a scheduled job every 15 minutes, picks refunds with status pending and next_check_at <= now. If provider_refund_id is known: fetch from provider (10s timeout, step 4 retry rules); succeeded or failed leads to transition (actor system:reconciler) with same effects as step 8 including email outbox; still pending leads to audit refund.status_checked and next_check_at = now plus interval growing from 1h to max 6h. If queued/unconfirmed/expired-lease submitting: if first_submitted_at is empty or under about 22 hours ago, resend with same key and handle as step 5; if window has run out, stay pending and search the provider's refunds for the charge by metadata.our_refund_id. Also retries matching unmatched webhook events. If provider unavailable: leave row unchanged, next_check_at = now + 15 min. Alert support if pending more than 3 days or an unconfirmed refund can't be found after the key window.
sonnet.q11: The server returns 202 with the refund id, and the page shows the refund as "Pending – sending to provider" and polls GET /admin/refunds/:id every few seconds. After the provider's immediate answer it shows "Pending – accepted by provider, waiting for final result" (accepted), "Failed" with the provider's message (4xx), or "Pending – provider did not confirm, we are checking automatically" (unconfirmed).
